rationale: Three lenses ran (blind, edge-case, acceptance) over a 905-line code diff. One critical defect is confirmed independently by all three: _load_overrides folds _switchless_defaults into every stored row, so a declaration's neutral values are laid over YAML for components that DO exist in YAML. Two concrete reproductions exist against shipped config, and it fails AC2 outright. Five further actionable findings: a save-triggered window where synchronous readers revert to YAML, an eager per-call rebuild of the runtime component list in hot paths, a hot-spin risk when the TTL is <= 0, two missing AC12 tests, and a code-quality guide violation. Commit format passes on all 11 commits; no secrets or unsafe execution surface in the diff. Dismissed as unreachable or pre-existing: the runtime-id YAML fallback (all six CONFIG_IDS are always emitted), the staticmethod-wrapped validate_id (carried over verbatim from main), and _expires_at not advancing on a failed load (pre-existing). Deferred and noted, not emitted: processes that import customer_config without running the FastAPI lifespan see an empty snapshot permanently, a design limit worth recording in the spec.

business_review.note: Single resolver in configs/component_resolution.py used by both the sync path (customer_config.py:232-246) and /v1/config (customer_config_service.py:146-155).
customer_config_service.py:126 folds _switchless_defaults into every row; neutral values overwrite YAML. See CR-001.
Missing key resolves to False; test_customer_config.py:186 unchanged and still passing.
reset_setting clears the snapshot so sync readers fall back to YAML; no backend-side test (see CR-004).
component_resolution.py:99-100 returns the runtime component before consulting the snapshot.
No call site touched; all 21 flag reads keep their synchronous signatures.
Refresh loop scheduled independently of /v1/config; interval from override_cache.ttl_seconds.
Warm-up awaited at main.py:809 before _initialize_optional_features() and before yield; failure leaves the service on YAML.
get() serves the last good snapshot on load failure; refresh_overrides uses expire_now, not invalidate.
WEB_SEARCH declared; both branches covered at the call site; the frontend surface already reads features:webSearch.
Missing an end-to-end test for a stored row omitting a declared field, and a test that reset returns sync resolution to YAML. See CR-004.

standards_review.notes: All 11 commits match EPMCDME-14705: Description; the revert keeps its generated subject.
customer_config.py:135 introduces Optional[Component]; the guide requires X | None. This is the rule EPMCDME-13983 failed its first review round on. See CR-006.
make license-check clean; headers added to the 5 new test files.
No secrets, credentials, injection surface, or unsafe process/file handling in the diff.
The pilot ships a call-site test exercising both branches of enable_web_search at toolkit_service.py:260, previously untested.

findings.problem: _load_overrides stores `_switchless_defaults(declaration) | parsed`, so a declaration's neutral per-field values are merged into the override map for components that already exist in YAML. apply_override then lays them over the YAML settings.
findings.impact: Two reproductions against shipped config. (a) releaseNotesRecentCount declares no `enabled` field, so the fold injects enabled=False over YAML's enabled: true — saving the release-notes count from the admin UI drops the component from GET /v1/config and makes is_component_enabled return False, while list_settings still shows the saved value so the admin never sees it. (b) A row written before a declaration gained a field resolves that field to '' instead of the YAML value. Both are regressions against main and violate AC2, the criterion per-field resolution exists for.
findings.recommendation: Keep `overrides[component_id] = parsed`. The neutral defaults are only needed for a component YAML omits, which component_resolution._from_override_alone already handles by defaulting enabled to False. If per-field neutral values are still wanted there, pass them to the resolver as a separate map consulted only in that branch. Add resolve_components tests for both reproductions.

findings.problem: OverrideCache.invalidate() now calls component_resolution.clear_snapshot(), and invalidate() is what save_setting and reset_setting call after a write. The snapshot is the only source synchronous readers have.
findings.impact: Immediately after an admin saves any setting, every override — not just the saved one — disappears for synchronous readers on the writing pod until the next get(), up to a full TTL later. An admin who disabled web search and then saves anything re-enables it in chat for that window. Worse, if the database is unreachable during that window _loaded is False, so get() returns {} and the pod stays on YAML indefinitely, having discarded a good snapshot — exactly the degradation the class docstring promises to avoid.
findings.recommendation: Have the write path reload rather than wipe: call `await refresh_overrides()` after a successful write (save_setting and reset_setting are both async), or make invalidate() reset only the freshness state and leave the snapshot as the degradation fallback.

findings.problem: resolve_component evaluates self._get_runtime_config() unconditionally on every call, before the resolver checks whether the id is even runtime-computed. That call runs importlib.metadata.version('codemie-enterprise') — raising and catching PackageNotFoundError on non-enterprise deployments — and constructs six Component/ComponentSetting models.
findings.impact: Every feature-flag read on a request path became a distribution-metadata scan plus twelve pydantic validations. Measured at roughly 76 microseconds per call against a previous plain list scan. toolkit_service performs three such checks per chat request, and assistant_handlers, workflow.py, project_service and tool_permissions_service add more.
findings.recommendation: Build the runtime list only when it can matter: `runtime = self._get_runtime_config() if component_id in runtime_ids else []` in resolve_component, or memoise _get_runtime_config, whose inputs do not change during the process lifetime.

findings.problem: AC12 is only partly covered. There is no end-to-end test for a stored row that omits a declared field (test_component_resolution.py:53 exercises an undeclared field at resolver level only), and no test that reset returns backend synchronous resolution to YAML (test_customer_config_audit.py:104 asserts invalidate was called, with the real implementation mocked out).
findings.impact: These are precisely the two paths where CR-001 lives and where a future change to invalidate/clear_snapshot would silently break the reset guarantee. The critical defect shipped through a green suite because neither path is tested.
findings.recommendation: Add a resolve_components test with a legacy row missing a declared field asserting the YAML value survives, and a test asserting that after reset_setting customer_config.is_feature_enabled falls back to YAML.

findings.problem: The refresh loop sleeps for override_cache.ttl_seconds, taken verbatim from CUSTOMER_CONFIG_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, a plain int with no lower bound that is environment-overridable.
findings.impact: A TTL of 0 — a plausible reading of 'disable caching' — makes asyncio.sleep return immediately, turning the background task into a hot loop that queries Postgres continuously and saturates the connection pool. Nothing bounds the rate, because _warm_customer_config swallows every exception so even a failing database does not slow it down.
findings.recommendation: Clamp the sleep to at least one second, or constrain the config field with a lower bound.

findings.problem: resolve_component is annotated Optional[Component]. .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md requires X | None unions rather than typing.Optional.
findings.impact: A documented project standard, and the specific rule the EPMCDME-13983 review failed on in its first round, so it will be raised again by a human reviewer.
findings.recommendation: Use Component | None. The surrounding file predates the rule, but new signatures should follow it.
